title: Pilot Semester vs Full-Year Drone Programs: How Schools Start Small
sub_heading: When a evaluation semester makes sense, what to measure before district rollout, and how seat caps and terms usually align.
body_html:
Draft — review before import. Do not publish until leadership approves tier language.

In short: Many districts start with a pilot semester—one section, one teacher, clear success metrics—before committing to a full-year or multi-site program. This article compares pilot vs classroom-year models without public B2B pricing.

Pilot semester (evaluation)

  • One teacher, typically 25–30 students
  • 90 days or one semester from launch
  • Goal: prove adoption, dashboard use, and exam participation
  • Success signals: active weekly usage, unit exam completion, teacher satisfaction

Full-year classroom

  • Aligned to district calendar; larger seat caps
  • Mid-year check-in and renewal planning
  • Good when CTE pathway is already approved

What to measure during a pilot

Track enrollment vs active students, units completed by week 6, unit exam attempts, and manager dashboard login frequency. Avoid promising FAA pass rates as a pilot KPI unless the school defines that independently.

Questions answered

Can we expand seats mid-pilot?

Usually via add-on quote—confirm with sales during scoping.

Does a pilot include onboarding?

Yes—a manager onboarding call is standard for school packages.
